advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the hosted-OpenAI default flip from `openai-chat:` to `openai-responses:` (a changed default altering existing configs' wire protocol) is an intended, documented pre-v1 change with the `openai-chat:` migration path, not an accidental break.
evidence: `_openai_target` returns `openai-responses:` by default: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:228 `return f"openai-chat:{tail}" if endpoint else f"openai-responses:{tail}"`
Inference path now flips: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:293-294 `if inferred == "openai": return _openai_target(model, endpoint=endpoint)` (previously `inferred = "openai-chat"`)
`_pai_model` bare/inferred openai now uses `_openai_wire_prefix`: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:213-214 and anthropic_model.py:219-223 (`return "openai-chat" if base_url else "openai-responses"`)

Consumer of the resolved string that keyed on the old default is updated, not broken: tests/external/_live_llm.py:60-63 `_PROVIDER_FAMILY_BY_QUALIFIER` now maps both `openai-chat` and `openai-responses` to family `openai`

Migration path + deprecation are provided: src/rebar/_deprecations.py:112 `_scheduled("cfg", "the hosted-OpenAI 'openai-chat:' provider prefix", "'openai-responses:'")` and docs/llm-framework.md:169-174 document setting explicit `openai-chat:` to retain Chat Completions
Pre-v1 project: deprecation `remove_in` is v1.0.0 (docs/config-reference.md:160), so this is an intentional unversioned pre-v1 default change with a documented migration path
advisory.finding: The default wire protocol for hosted OpenAI changed: an existing config of `model = "gpt-4o"`, `model = "openai:gpt-4o"`, or `model_provider = "openai"` (with no custom base_url) previously resolved to `openai-chat:` (Chat Completions) and now resolves to `openai-responses:` (Responses API), silently altering the request/response wire shape for existing operator configurations.
scenarios: An operator with an existing `model_provider = "openai"` / bare `gpt-4o` config and only OPENAI_API_KEY set: their next run switches from /v1/chat/completions to /v1/responses without any config change on their part.

evidence: src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:228 `return f"openai-chat:{tail}" if endpoint else f"openai-responses:{tail}"` — bare/inferred openai now defaults to Responses

Consumer configs affected: `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml:25` uses explicit `openai-chat:` (unaffected), but docs/llm-example-configs.md:61,94 and docs/llm-framework.md:238,257,274 show bare `gpt-4o` / model-class usage whose resolution flips

Migration path present: registered deprecation src/rebar/_deprecations.py:112 (remove_in v1.0.0), documented in docs/llm-framework.md:148-174, explicit `openai-chat:` opt-out preserved (tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:169-172)
advisory.finding: Changed default wire protocol on a public config surface: an existing hosted-OpenAI config expressed as a bare/inferred `openai` (`model = "gpt-4o"`, `model = "openai:gpt-4o"`, or `model_provider = "openai"` with no custom base_url) now resolves to `openai-responses:` (Responses API) instead of `openai-chat:` (Chat Completions). This silently changes the request/response wire shape for configs that were valid before. It is deprecation-guarded and documented with an explicit `openai-chat:` opt-out, so a migration path exists, but the default flip affects unchanged existing configs.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `ProviderSession(...).is_resolvable('openai-responses') is True` (and that `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` contains `openai-responses`), pinning the gate the default flip relies on.
evidence: Docstring states the intent: 'Listed here so `is_resolvable("openai-responses")` is True and rebar leaves it a lazy model STRING for pydantic-ai to build'

tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:364-375 `test_every_inferred_provider_name_is_resolvable` parametrizes over `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` (the inference table, which maps bare ids to `openai`, not `openai-responses`), so it never asserts `is_resolvable('openai-responses')`
tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:336 asserts only `_pydantic_ai_known_providers() <= KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (a subset direction), not that it CONTAINS `openai-responses`

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `is_resolvable` and `_EXTRA_KNOWN_PROVIDERS` across tests returns no assertion of `is_resolvable('openai-responses') is True`; the migration runner tests (tests/unit/test_openai_responses_migration.py:66-77) use `model_override=FunctionModel(...)`, which bypasses ProviderSession resolution entirely
blocking.finding: The newly added `_EXTRA_KNOWN_PROVIDERS = frozenset({'openai-responses'})` / `| _EXTRA_KNOWN_PROVIDERS` union in providers.py — whose sole purpose is to make `is_resolvable('openai-responses')` return True so the default-flipped `openai-responses:` targets survive provider resolution — has no test asserting that resolvability. If `openai-responses` were dropped from the extra set, every default-flipped hosted OpenAI target would fail at construction, and no test in this diff would catch it.
